references.text: The original list of materials to be gathered for the tabernacle included blue and purple wool, crimson thread, and fine linen.
Mentions red-dyed ram skins and badger skins as materials for the tabernacle, the same materials listed in Exodus 35:23.
Goat hair was used to make coverings over the tabernacle, which explains why goat hair was gathered.
Describes the use of red-dyed ram skins and badger skins as a covering over the tabernacle.
A parallel verse listing the same materials that were to be brought as offerings.
The skilled women spun the blue and purple wool, the crimson thread, the fine linen, and the goat hair.
The materials were used to make the covering of red-dyed ram skins and badger skins over the tabernacle.
Badger skins were used to cover the ark of the covenant during transport.
David gathered materials for the temple, including many of the same fabrics that were used for the tabernacle.
The same holy materials are used both for the furnishings of the tabernacle (35:23) and for the high priest's garments (28:5), showing the unity of God's plan for worship.
This is a direct continuation of the list in 35:23; together they describe all the materials (skins and wood) that were brought for the roof and structure of the sanctuary.
This shows the result of the givers' actions: the materials brought in 35:23 ended up as the protective covering over the tabernacle in 39:24.
The connection between the givers' materials (35:23) and the recipients' divine wisdom to work them (35:35) shows that both material resources and creativity are God's gifts.
This shows who worked the materials that people brought in 35:23; Oholiab was one of the chosen artisans who worked with these specific fabrics.
The same holy colors and fabrics gathered in 35:23 were used to make the high priest's belt, showing the unity of God's plan for both the house and its service.
